description:
Senior Associate, People Team

Coefficient Giving is growing fast, and how we work is changing. Now is an unusually high-leverage moment to help build the People side of our organization: the structure, systems, and everyday experience that enable our team to do its best work on some of the world's most pressing problems. What you build today will shape how CG works for years to come.

We're hiring at least one Senior Associate across our People Operations and Global Employment teams. We'll work together to figure out which team suits you best and shape the role around the person we hire.

About Coefficient Giving

Coefficient Giving is a philanthropic funder and advisor. Since 2014, we’ve directed over $8 billion in grants as part of our mission to help others as much as we can with the resources available to us. It's also a pivotal moment for Coefficient Giving: we gave around $1 billion last year, and have more than tripled our giving this year. We work with a range of donors who share our commitment to cost-effective, high-impact giving. Our current funds include Science and Global Health R&D, Navigating Transformative Artificial Intelligence, Abundance & Growth, Farm Animal Welfare, Biosecurity & Pandemic Preparedness, and more.

We’re proud of our track record:

  • Our grants to evidence-backed global health programs have saved over 100,000 lives, and our farm animal welfare grants have improved the lives of over 3 billion animals.

  • We supported late-stage clinical trials for the R21 malaria vaccine, now being scaled to protect millions of kids globally.

  • We were the earliest major funder of the YIMBY movement to build more housing. Our grantees have led the charge on major wins like City of Yes in New York, and SB 79 in California, which will enable hundreds of thousands of new housing units.

  • We jump-started the field of AI safety and security and have played a vital role in addressing other existential threats, such as mirror bacteria.

About the People team

CG's People team consists of three sub-teams (Recruiting, People Operations, and Global Employment) that report to Stephanie Hill. These three sub-teams are responsible for the full life cycle of an employee , from "we think we need a person" to their last day. We’re hiring for roles on our People Operations and Global Employment teams.

  • People Operations looks after teammates’ experience once they're here: onboarding and offboarding, performance reviews and growth, engagement surveys, and employee support. It's a team of four, led by Gabriella Plevin.

  • Global Employment ensures CG can employ people compliantly and competitively wherever they're based: in the US, the UK, and 15+ other countries through our employer of record. The team handles contracts, pay, benefits, leave, business immigration, and employment policy. It's a team of six, led by Zoë Johannas.

The two teams work closely, and much of their work overlaps. For example, a new hire's first few weeks depend on People Ops getting onboarding right, and Global Employment getting their contract, payroll, and benefits right. We share HiBob as our people system, and both teams are building it out as we grow.

In the last six months, the People Ops and Global Employment teams have:

  • Moved performance reviews, onboarding, and employment changes into HiBob

  • Cut new hire setup from one hour to one minute

  • Executed two-day turnarounds from offer-in-hand to first day of work for urgent roles

  • Shortened our performance review cycle from 75–90 days to 16 days

  • Set up Coefficient Giving UK as its own employer, allowing us to move UK staff off our employer of record and onto a new UK benefits package

  • Run this year's compensation and leveling updates, using AI tools and our HiBob integration

  • Transitioned to a new immigration firm to speed up and improve visa processing and support

  • Hired in nine new countries; we now have staff in 21 different countries across six continents (excluding Antarctica)

What you might work on

We're hiring for two broad profiles. Though there’s a lot of overlap, each profile suits a slightly different skillset. You don't need to pick one when you apply, but we'll ask which you're most excited about and whether there's one you'd rather not do.

People Operations. This profile is a good fit if you like building and fixing processes and systems, and making them work well for staff and managers. Examples of work you might own:

  • Running our performance review cycles in HiBob, from launch to calibration

  • Making HiBob work well for staff: workflows, guides, and reports

  • Engagement surveys, from setup to clean data

  • Onboarding and offboarding at 20+ new people a month

  • Projects to cut or automate work we still do by hand

Whoever joins this profile will take on some of our recurring performance review and HiBob work.

Global Employment. This profile is a good fit if you're precise and detail-obsessed about pay, benefits, and compliance, and you like being someone who gets it right every time. Examples of work you might own:

  • Payroll changes and checks across our US entities, Coefficient Giving UK, and our employer of record

  • Benefits admin and open enrollment, and being the first stop for benefits and leave questions

  • Keeping employment data in HiBob (titles, levels, reporting lines and pay) accurate as people's roles change

  • Contracts, onboarding and offboarding for international hires

  • Keeping our employment policies and handbooks up to date

  • Building systems for scale, like a request ticketing system for HR questions

Whoever joins this profile will take on some of the day-to-day pay, benefits, and leave work that currently runs through Nick Ravazzolo, our Global Employment Manager.

Across both roles, you'd use AI tools as a normal part of your work, and you'd be responsible for identifying opportunities for process improvement.

What it's like to work here

CG is moving fast, and the People team’s work actively supports that. We're onboarding 20+ people a month, building systems that didn't exist a year ago, and changing how we do things whenever we find a better way. Priorities can shift week to week, and you may need to drop something you've worked hard on when something more important comes along.

We hold a very high bar for performance. Great, reliable work is the baseline here, not the thing that sets you apart. We don't expect crazy hours, and we take sustainability seriously (we recommend four or more weeks of paid leave a year, on top of public holidays). But there are busy stretches, like a performance review cycle, open enrollment, or a hiring push, when working more is necessary.

In return, our staff receive a lot of trust and room to run. We treat each other like adults: few rules, flexible hours, direct feedback in every direction, and very little bureaucratic faff. Our goal for internal operations is that "CG just works," and the People team is a big part of making that true.

Level

This is a Senior Associate role. You'd run important, recurring workstreams and make them better over time. You'd get a clear sense of priorities from your manager, then own the execution: spotting what's breaking, fixing it, and documenting what you changed. You'd sometimes lead a bigger project from start to finish within an area someone else leads. At this level, candidates typically have ~3 to 5 years in people operations, HR, operations, or a systems-heavy role.

Who might be a good fit

  • You have deep experience in at least one part of people or employment operations, and range beyond it. For the People Ops profile, that might include past experience running performance cycles, owning an HRIS like HiBob, onboarding at volume, or running engagement surveys. For the Global Employment profile, that might include US payroll and benefits administration, multi-state or UK employment compliance, working with an employer of record, or supporting compensation reviews. International employment experience is a big plus.

  • You care about CG's mission, including our work on navigating transformative AI. You should be following AI risk at least casually. Ideally, you take AI risk seriously, can explain in your own words why it matters, and want to work somewhere that’s acting on it.

  • You take ownership. You notice what's broken before anyone asks, find the most efficient fix, and see it through. You 80/20 the things that don't need to be perfect and take real pride in the things that do. You're not above unglamorous work, since a lot of what makes people operations great is getting the small things right every time.

  • You're incredibly on it. You're fast, reliable, and detail-obsessed, and people trust you with confidential data. Colleagues can hand you something and stop thinking about it.

  • You do well with pace and change. You can hold a lot of moving parts, reprioritize quickly when something more important comes up, and stay calm and kind when things get busy. If CG needs to sprint, you're up for it, and you can pivot fast when the teams we support do.

  • You give and want direct feedback. You'll tell us when a process isn't working, even if we built it. The teams we support hold a high bar and will tell you when something could be faster or simpler. You find that useful, not deflating; you accept critique of your work without taking it personally, and you change your mind when the evidence suggests you should.

  • You communicate clearly and concisely, mostly in writing. We write more than we meet. You know how to assign clear directives, without burying them in complicated explanations. You have strong reasoning transparency and are honest about what you know and what you don’t.

  • You use AI tools ambitiously and critically. You reach for automation and AI by default — but you check the output, because getting someone's pay or benefits wrong isn't acceptable.

  • You're low ego, and you care about people. You share credit easily, you care about the staff you're supporting, and you care more about CG working well than about guarding your own lane.

The ideal candidate will have many — but probably not all — of these characteristics. There's no single background we are looking for. If the mandate excites you, we strongly encourage you to apply.

Why you might not want this role

We think it's valuable to share what you may not enjoy about this role so you can make an educated decision before spending time on an application:

  • It's fast and busy, with high expectations all the time. If you're looking for a steady, predictable role where you can settle into a routine, this probably isn't it.

  • A meaningful share of the work is recurring and operational. Review cycles, payroll checks, benefits questions, and HiBob requests don't go away, and someone has to own them and do them well. We'll keep automating what we can, but if you mainly want to focus on strategy and design, this role may frustrate you.

  • The shape of the role will keep shifting. CG is growing fast, the line between People Ops and Global Employment work will always be a little bit fuzzy, and you often have to drop or reshape work when something more important comes along. If you need a tightly defined scope, that's hard to promise at this time.

  • You'll be in service of other teams' priorities. Much of the job is making things easier for other people, which can feel unglamorous or far away from the broader organizational mission.

  • We're not heavy on formal training or career planning. You'll learn a lot from the work and your colleagues, and your manager will take your growth seriously, but we can't map out where this role leads in five years.

  • We work across a lot of time zones. The People team is spread across the US, the UK, and beyond, so you'll need some overlap with US hours and should be comfortable working mostly asynchronously and in writing.

Role details and benefits

  • Compensation: The baseline compensation for this role is $134,550, which would be distributed as a base salary of $117,000 and an unconditional 401(k) grant of $17,550 for U.S. hires. All compensation will be distributed in the form of take-home salary for internationally-based hires.

    • These compensation figures assume a remote location; there would be geographic adjustments upwards for candidates who are based in the San Francisco Bay Area or Washington, D.C. and are willing to work from our local office approximately two days per week or more.

    • There would also be an adjustment upwards for candidates based in New York who are willing to work from our coworking hub at least one day per week.

  • Time zones and location: We offer remote work in many countries. We are open to hires outside the U.S. who can consistently overlap with U.S. business hours for at least 5 hours a day.

  • Benefits: Our benefits package includes:

    • Time off: Flexible PTO with no cap. We encourage ~23 days plus 12 holidays, about seven weeks a year.

    • Family: 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave (birth, adoption, or foster placement), a fertility and family-forming benefit, 20 days of backup dependent care, and a Day Care FSA.

    • Productivity and growth: A $10,000 annual productivity benefit (pro-rated in the year you start), a generous expense policy for the equipment, software, and services you need, and paid professional development.

    • Health (U.S.): We pay 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for you and your family, plus life and disability insurance and up to $5,000/year through a Health Reimbursement Arrangement for out-of-pocket costs.

    • Workspace: Offices in San Francisco and Washington, D.C., coworking hubs in New York and London, or a coworking membership wherever you’re based.

    • Outside the U.S.: Where we can’t offer a core benefit locally, we take a country-specific approach so all staff get the same or equivalent benefits.

  • Start date: We’d like a candidate to start as soon as possible after receiving an offer — and definitely no later than the end of February, though ideally sooner.

We aim to employ people with many different experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds who share our passion for accomplishing as much good as we can. We are committed to creating an environment where all employees have the opportunity to succeed, and we do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected status.

If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, or have any other questions about applying, please contact jobs@coefficientgiving.org.

Please apply by 11:59 p.m. EST on Sunday, December 6 2026 to be considered.

U.S.-based staff are typically employed by Coefficient Giving LLC, which is not a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization. As such, this role is unlikely to be eligible for Public Service Loan Forgiveness programs.

We may use AI to assist in the initial screening of applications, including to detect whether candidates have used AI models in drafting their application. Decisions are always made by a human on our team.

If you have any questions about our use of AI tools, you can email jobs@coefficientgiving.org.
